The Ignition Pass is a Residency grant for early-stage Tough Tech startups.
In collaboration with Shell, a leader in the future of energy, The Engine will jointly select up to five startups whose technologies align with strategic energy priorities.
Selected startups will receive business support, expert mentorship, and funding for up to one year of Residency at The Engine.
While startups are not required to be founded in the Boston area, they must be registered in the United States.
Must not have raised more than $10 million of capital (excluding non-dilutive funding) or have trailing 12-month revenue of more than $3 million.
Early-stage Tough Tech companies developing physical technologies in the technology areas mentioned above.

Ready to Accelerate Your Tough Tech Startup?
Apply for the second Ignition Pass to access up to one year of funded Residency, specialized lab and engineering facilities, and Shell’s technical experts.
What is the award value of The Ignition Pass?

The Ignition Pass award value varies based on team size and is designed to cover the cost of access to BSL2 lab benches, engineering benches, high bay fabrication floor space, more than 1,880 pieces of shared lab equipment, and customized infrastructure support at The Engine.
The Ignition Pass is for early-stage startup teams with an immediate need to develop or commercialize their technology that require specialized facilities.

Get Involved What is Tough Tech?
Tough Tech has the potential to change the world — but only if it makes it out of the lab.
Our Approach: We provide innovative founders with the necessary resources, infrastructure, and access to the Tough Tech ecosystem to fuel their growth.
By convening policymakers, investors, and founders, we align the Tough Tech ecosystem to drive progress towards solving the world’s most important challenges.
Our Story MIT created The Engine in 2016 to support Tough Tech startups poised to deliver meaningful, positive impact on society and the environment.
Initially combining an incubator with a venture capital fund, The Engine provided early-stage companies with capital, infrastructure, and operational support.
In 2023, Engine Ventures spun out as a separate investment firm focused on Tough Tech companies.

In 2025, The Engine formally became a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, expanding its commitment to supporting Tough Tech companies and ecosystems nationwide through specialized programming, shared lab and engineering infrastructure, and a network designed to help companies move from scientific breakthroughs to commercial impact.
We believe success in this mission is achieved through humility in the face of the unknown and dedication in championing the Tough Tech community.
We share our wins and our learnings to accelerate the path of the Tough Tech community we support.
Anyone with the technical chops and ambition to drive change could be a Tough Tech founder or funder.

Frequently Asked Questions What are The Engine’s programs for Resident Tough Tech companies?
Does The Engine provide mentorship to companies in the Residency program?
The Engine connects Resident companies with a network of mentors, including investors, veteran Tough Tech entrepreneurs, and The Engine’s experts in residence.
These mentors offer expertise across talent, public affairs, legal guidance, finance, communication, and leadership, tailored to each company’s technical and commercial goals.
These programs provide both technical and business insight needed to support Tough Tech commercialization.
